aiSummary.oneLiner: A multimodal AI agent framework that interprets visual charts and market news for financial trading.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: Vibe-Trading introduces a novel multimodal trading framework that leverages Large Multimodal Models (LMMs) to make complex financial decisions. It moves beyond traditional quantitative analysis by allowing AI agents to visually interpret financial charts, read breaking market news, and analyze social media sentiment—capturing the 'vibe' of the market. The system integrates real-time data feeds and employs specialized agents for distinct tasks, such as technical chart analysis and fundamental news summarization. By synthesizing these diverse inputs, the framework aims to execute more nuanced and context-aware algorithmic trading strategies.
keyFeatures: Multimodal Analysis: Natively processes visual candlestick charts alongside textual market news and social sentiment.
Multi-Agent Architecture: Utilizes distinct, specialized LLM agents for technical analysis, fundamental analysis, and final trade execution.
Real-Time Data Integration: Connects to live financial APIs to fetch the latest price action and breaking market updates.
Explainable Decisions: Generates detailed, human-readable reasoning logs explaining the rationale behind every trading signal.
Backtesting Engine: Includes tools to simulate trading strategies against historical market data to validate performance.

releases.name: v0.1.19 — research that outlives the chat
releases.body:
Rolls up 299 commits / 116 merged pull requests since 0.1.18, plus 21
pull requests whose work landed through maintainer commits, from 26
contributors.

The headline is research that outlives the chat that produced it. A finished
analysis can be saved as a versioned research artifact with its evidence
references and data-as-of date, searched later, and revised instead of
overwritten; a follow-up turn or a later session finds the backtests already
run through `list_backtest_runs` and reads their artifacts instead of running
them again; and a research goal's objective can be edited without losing its
evidence. Paper trading adds an opt-in A-share five-minute simulation that
settles a completed session bar by bar on a new order lifecycle, with
JoinQuant's limit-fill rules; saved accounts still settle daily. Gildata
financial queries, report-period stock screening and Shannon portfolio
diagnosis arrive as separate opt-ins for Gildata account holders, Gildata
quotes are used only when named, and the QVeris integration is removed.
Argentina (BYMA shares and CEDEARs) joins as a backtest market, `web_search`
can use Parallel's hosted search, and Codex OAuth lists the models the
signed-in a

releases.name: v0.1.18 — lean runtime and reliability fixes
releases.body:
Same-day follow-up to 0.1.17: 12 commits (10 non-merge), no new external pull
requests. It ships the fixes made on main after 0.1.17 — `mcp>=1.30` so the
HTTP MCP transport reclaims sessions, connect-time checks for custom model
endpoints (including fake-IP proxy hosts), grounding of `run_dir/…` refs and
signed amounts, Beijing codes in correlation, the macOS timeout fix and the
sdist contents — together with a leaner agent runtime: tool schemas load on
demand through `load_tools`, oversized tool results stay readable in the run
directory, Swarm sizes its context by the model window, and usage accounting
covers compaction, cancelled responses and failed streams. On the 0.1.17
pre-release verification prompt (DeepSeek V4 Pro, a 20/60 SMA backtest on
AAPL.US) a run took 7 model calls instead of 12 and 152K input tokens instead
of 706K, and reported the same figures.

### Known issues

- A retried provider error (a connection reset or rate limit) can halt live
  model decisions until the next UTC day, and a research goal's final answer
  that crosses its token budget is discarded. Both are fixed on main (see
  Unreleased) and ship with the next release.

### Changed

- Reduce agent r

releases.name: v0.1.17 — paper accounts, and a value that cannot be computed says so
releases.body:
Rolls up 638 commits / 228 merged pull requests since 0.1.16, plus 41 pull
requests whose work landed through maintainer commits, from 33 contributors.

The headline is daily paper trading. A `paper_trade_step` tool for the agent
and MCP, and saved paper accounts through `vibe-trading paper`,
`/api/paper-accounts` and a Web page, match orders or a strategy against
completed daily bars without ever reaching a broker; saved accounts move
forward only. Most of
the rest of the cycle is correctness, and much of it has one shape: a value
that cannot be computed now says so instead of turning into a plausible
number. A profit factor with no losing trade, an undefined correlation, a
factor benchmark with too few IC observations, an upside at a zero price and
an unbounded ratio come back as `null` or a refusal rather than 0; a missing
price no longer bridges a return pair, a VaR transition or a lag pair; an
after-close SEC filing no longer reaches the IC a bar early; and a misspelled
backtest setting is reported in the run card instead of silently ignored.
Brazil (B3) joins as a market, the Alpha Zoo grows from 462 to 478 factors,
Slack and Discord join the guided channel setup, scheduled

releases.name: v0.1.16 — a number that can show where it came from
releases.body:
Rolls up 492 commits / 116 merged pull requests since 0.1.15, from 16
contributors.

The theme of this cycle is a number that can show where it came from. The
final-answer grounding gate stopped guessing what a number is from the words
around it: the model declares each figure's role — observed, derived,
proposed, cited or count — the gate checks that declaration against the
session's tool evidence, and a figure that fails is cut from the answer
instead of the whole answer being refused. A backtest's own output (its
Sortino, turnover, weights and Monte Carlo p-values, not only its Sharpe)
now grounds the report written about it, run cards cite a metric only where
the saved CSV agrees, and the generated broker matrix states each profile's
permissions as declarations rather than as runtime verification. Research
runs stopped losing what they fetched: compaction follows the model's real
context window instead of a fixed 40K estimate that began clearing tool
results from the third step. The missing-data sweep reached 59 more alphas:
15 qlib158 count factors, 20 that filled a missing input with a constant
and 24 comparison gates. Argentina (BYMA), weekly and monthly bars, Bahasa
Indones

releases.name: v0.1.15 — data that says what it is
releases.body:
Rolls up 551 commits / 162 merged pull requests since 0.1.14, from 35
contributors.

The theme of this cycle is data that says what it is. A price frame now
carries the adjustment caliber it was served under. A factor propagates the
gaps in its inputs instead of filling them. A loader that cannot serve a
market no longer claims it, and a source that fails to refresh is an error
rather than a smaller portfolio. Three of those were the same bug wearing
different clothes: a default that silently substitutes a plausible value for
a missing one, which is indistinguishable downstream from a real
observation. Three new markets, a fourteenth broker and fifteen Quant
Library additions land alongside.

### Added

- **UK equity market** (#1206, thanks @cgycorey) — LSE `.L` and `.IL`
  symbols end to end: market data, Yahoo-backed financial statements and
  indicators, trade-journal inference into `uk_equity`, and its own engine
  path. SDRT is modelled as what it actually is — a 0.5% duty on the
  **purchase** side only, not a symmetric round-trip cost. Charging both
  sides overstated the cost of every round trip by half, which is exactly
  the size of edge a mean-reversion strategy lives on

✨ Key Features


💡 What Is Vibe-Trading?

Vibe-Trading turns finance questions into research reports, runnable backtests and paper portfolios. You can also authorize a supported broker to execute live trades within a mandate you set and can halt. Your funds stay with the broker.

✨ What You Can Do

Task Where to start
Research markets, filings or uploaded documents Ask in Web chat or attach a report.
Backtest a strategy or benchmark alphas Inspect charts and trades in Run Detail, or compare factors in /alpha-zoo.
Simulate trading or replay a journal Track daily fills and NAV in /paper-trading. Use /journal and /shadow in the CLI to review your trades.
Combine accounts or compare allocations Open /portfolio for holdings and proposed allocation changes. Broker support
Explore options and correlations Open /options for multi-leg payoffs and Greeks, or /correlation for market regimes.
Coordinate or repeat research Run a Swarm team, assign work in Pixel Office or schedule a brief in /scheduled.
Revisit research with dated evidence Search /research-artifacts, compare any two revisions, and export a full series or selected comparison as JSON or Markdown. Versioned research

⚡ Quick Example

Once you have run vibe-trading init, you can ask for a backtest in plain English or benchmark an existing alpha library from the terminal.

vibe-trading run -p "Backtest a BTC-USDT 20/50 moving-average crossover for 2024. Compare it with buy-and-hold and report maximum drawdown."
vibe-trading alpha bench --zoo gtja191 --universe csi300 --period 2018-2025 --top 20

Open Run Detail to compare the crossover with buy-and-hold, inspect the trades behind a drawdown and check the data source on the run card.

🧪 Research Workflow

Step In the crossover example
Plan Identify the trading pair, date range, moving averages and benchmark from the prompt.
Ground Fetch historical bars for BTC-USDT. Check the source and dates before interpreting the result.
Execute Write the strategy and run the backtest. The run directory holds the strategy, trades and equity curve.
Validate Compare the result with buy-and-hold. Inspect turnover, drawdown and validation warnings alongside return.
Revisit Open the saved run or ask a follow-up with different parameters. You can also save a dated research conclusion and revise it when new evidence arrives.

📡 Data Sources & Smart Fallback

The loader supports 28 market-data sources. With source: "auto", it infers the market from the symbol and tries the configured sources in order.

Market How a request is filled
A-shares and Hong Kong Start with Tencent. If it cannot supply the bars, try Eastmoney and then the remaining sources for that market.
US equities Start with Yahoo. Stooq and Sina are the next two sources in the chain.
Crypto Try OKX, Binance and CCXT before falling back to other sources.
Futures Chinese contracts can use AKShare or local bars. Supply local bars for global contracts.

You can also choose a source explicitly. For example, installing vibe-trading-ai[ashare] adds the token-free BaoStock loader for daily A-share bars. The data source reference lists the full chains and credential requirements.

🔩 Detailed Capabilities

Market research

Feature What you can do
Filings and holdings Compare a manager’s SEC 13F holdings across quarters, or look through an ETF to its underlying positions. Each holdings report carries its reporting date.
Company valuation Use /dcf to see how a valuation changes with the discount rate and terminal growth. Use /comps for peer multiples, or build a linked three-statement model and export the results to Excel.
Papers and documents Search arXiv and OpenAlex for a signal, inspect the authors’ definition, then test it on your own universe. Upload a filing, spreadsheet or slide deck for questions about a specific exhibit.
Stock screening With Gildata enabled, screen companies by market cap and retrieve half-year revenue in one request. Screening and portfolio factor diagnosis each have their own opt-in.

Quant research

Feature What you can do
Alpha Zoo Benchmark signals from Qlib, Alpha101, GTJA and the academic and fundamental libraries. Compare information coefficients across horizons, then check whether the result survives a walk-forward test.
Backtest engines Model A-share price limits, crypto funding or futures margin. Use a shared capital pool for a cross-market strategy and inspect the individual fills behind its returns.
Options Lab Build a spread leg by leg. Compare its expiry payoff with the Greeks and see how the position responds to a change in spot price and implied volatility.
Portfolio risk Inspect drawdowns, estimate value at risk and expected shortfall, or use Brinson attribution to separate allocation from stock selection. The correlation view shows when markets start moving together.
Strategy tracking Register a strategy with its evidence and track how its Sharpe ratio or factor information coefficient changes as new results come in.

Accounts and trading

Feature What you can do
Portfolio Bring read-only broker holdings into one snapshot or import an extraETF export. Enter target weights to preview the value change for each holding.
Paper trading Advance a saved account one trading day and inspect fills, cash and NAV. You can also replay an A-share session in five-minute steps in a separate simulation. The paper_trade_reconcile agent/MCP tool independently checks fees, cash, positions and NAV arithmetic without market or broker access.
Shadow Account Import your broker’s trade journal, inspect fees and trading habits, then compare the actual trades with a rule-based replay.
Broker connections Set up a connection in the CLI or Web and test it with a read. For supported live profiles, set symbol, order and exposure limits before enabling trading. The kill switch halts live activity.

Teams and recurring research

Feature What you can do
Swarm and Pixel Office Run a bull–bear investment committee or a quant research desk and inspect the workers’ reports. In Pixel Office, assign a task to a teammate and record the result on the shared board.
Scheduled briefs Start from a premarket brief, an earnings tracker or a portfolio checkup. Choose a schedule and send the report to a configured channel such as Slack, Telegram or email.
Research history Search older sessions and reopen a saved run. Save a dated conclusion with its evidence and compare revisions when the investment case changes.
Run records Inspect the data source, model, execution record and metric references behind a backtest. Reopen the saved trades and equity curve to check a reported figure.

🚀 Quick Start

Terminal. Install the package with Python 3.11+, choose a model provider in the setup wizard, then open the interactive CLI.

pip install vibe-trading-ai
vibe-trading init
vibe-trading

Web app. Docker serves the frontend and API together at http://localhost:8899. From a fresh checkout, configure your provider before starting the container.

git clone https://github.com/HKUDS/Vibe-Trading.git
cd Vibe-Trading
cp agent/.env.example agent/.env
# Set your provider and API key in agent/.env.
docker compose up --build

The PyPI package includes the CLI, API and MCP server. For a frontend development setup or a local model, see the installation guide.

🖥 CLI Reference

Start vibe-trading for the interactive terminal. Type /help at the prompt to browse commands or use these shortcuts during research.

Command Use it to
/model Switch the provider or model for the session.
/history Browse and resume a prior conversation.
/show <run-id> Inspect the results of a saved run.
/pine Export the current strategy as a Pine Script indicator.

From the shell, vibe-trading alpha list browses the factor libraries and vibe-trading playbook list shows the scheduled research templates.

💡 Examples

  • Compare stocks. Ask “Compare AAPL and MSFT over 2024. Which month accounts for the largest gap in returns?” Resume the conversation later with /history.
  • Review your trades. Use /journal to analyze your exported trade history, then /shadow to compare your trades with a rule-based alternative.
  • Run an investment committee. Choose a stock and follow the bull and bear cases through to the final report.
vibe-trading --swarm-run investment_committee '{"target":"TSLA","market":"US"}'

🌐 API Server

Start a local server with vibe-trading serve --port 8899. In a second terminal, run curl http://localhost:8899/runs to list saved runs. Use the returned ID with GET /runs/{run_id} to inspect its results.

To run a research session over HTTP Endpoint
Create the conversation POST /sessions
Send the research question POST /sessions/{id}/messages
Follow progress as it happens GET /sessions/{id}/events

Open http://localhost:8899/docs to try the endpoints interactively. Authenticated clients send the API key in the Authorization: Bearer header.

🔌 MCP Plugin

MCP clients can launch the same package over stdio. Add this entry to Claude Desktop’s claude_desktop_config.json, restart the client and call list_skills.

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "vibe-trading": { "command": "vibe-trading-mcp" }
  }
}

For other clients or a custom output directory, see the MCP configurations.
